headline: A sunny but cool Saturday gives way to light rain Sunday evening around Los Angeles and a sunny, warmer Thanksgiving, but forecasters have significant concern for moderate to major coastal flooding along the beaches during Thanksgiving week.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Saturday is mostly sunny everywhere this afternoon once patchy low clouds over interior San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties clear by late morning; the morning Frost Advisories expired at 9 AM. North to northeast winds gusting 25 to 40 mph across the mountains and valleys this morning stay below advisory levels and die down this afternoon. Despite the sunshine, highs only reach the 60s in the Glendale area and elsewhere west of the mountains and the mid to upper 50s farther inland, about 4 to 8 degrees below normal. Saturday night stays dry.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: A weak cold front brings rain to most areas Sunday, reaching San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties in the afternoon and Ventura and Los Angeles counties in the evening. Amounts are light: up to a quarter inch on the Central Coast, maybe a tenth of an inch in the Los Angeles area and elsewhere south of Point Conception, and less than a tenth inland, with southerly winds ahead of the front warming things a degree or two. Monday is sunny and warmer, with highs in the mid 60s to lower 70s at the coast and in the valleys, and a morning push of northerly winds off the land brings gusts below advisory levels through and below north-south passes and canyons.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Tuesday stays dry but grows cloudier as the next weak storm approaches, with coast and valley highs in the upper 60s to lower 70s, about 2 to 4 degrees below normal. Rain arrives Tuesday night and ends by early Wednesday afternoon, with only a 20 to 30 percent chance south of Point Conception, including the Los Angeles area, and under a tenth of an inch if any; coastal San Luis Obispo County has a better than 70 percent chance (about 50 percent elsewhere on the Central Coast), with a tenth to a quarter inch there and up to half an inch north of Morro Bay. Thanksgiving and Black Friday are sunny, dry and warmer as high pressure builds, with possibly enough wind off the land for a moderate wind event; highs warm about 6 degrees on Thanksgiving and another 2 to 4 on Friday, reaching the 70s at all coasts and valleys, 5 to 10 degrees above normal.

coast: Forecasters have significant concern for moderate to major coastal flooding during Thanksgiving week, from a combination of unusually high sea levels (warm ocean water expands), very high spring tides with the moon near its closest point, and a large, long-period west swell. For the Central Coast, Ventura and Los Angeles county beaches, a Coastal Flood Advisory runs from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM Wednesday, followed by a Coastal Flood Watch from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon, when the swell arrives; peak high tides come between 8:45 and 10 AM at about 8.2–8.6 feet for Los Angeles and Ventura and 7.9–8.2 feet on the Central Coast, with a reasonable worst case 0.3–0.5 feet higher. If upgraded to a warning, flooding could reach farther inland and damage coastal roads and buildings, with significant beach erosion; places of greatest concern include Santa Monica to Palos Verdes, Long Beach/Naples, Faria to Silver Strand Beach and Ventura Harbor, and Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes and the Cayucos, Avila and Pismo piers. The Santa Barbara South Coast (Santa Barbara to Rincon and Jalama Beach) and the islands are under a Coastal Flood Advisory from 3 AM Monday to 3 PM Thursday, elevated to high surf is likely all week, and more coastal alerts will likely be needed Friday. Offshore, winds and seas stay below small craft advisory levels through the weekend; a significant west swell around 14 to 16 feet arrives midweek with large, hazardous seas on the outer waters, and advisory-level northwest to west winds are possible Wednesday and Wednesday night south of Point Conception.
watch_for: Moderate to major coastal flooding: the Coastal Flood Watch for Wednesday–Thursday morning high tides (8:45–10 AM) could be upgraded to a warning as the big swell arrives.
Light rain Sunday evening in Los Angeles County, around a tenth of an inch.
A possible moderate offshore wind event on Thanksgiving and Friday.
confidence: Forecasters say they have a good handle on the sunny, cool weekend and light Sunday rain; they describe the midweek storm as weak, and for the coast they say significant flooding impacts seem probable though exactly how the tides and swell line up is still somewhat uncertain.
